scope: Read-only source timing trace; no lag fitting, data changes or simulation.
conclusion: Source supports post-step state and forces from the SAME completed physics step. No intentional one-step ContactSensorData publication lag is present in the inspected chain. No posthoc force/state shift is justified.

chain.meaning: Physics Update performs UpdatePhysics, Step(dt), ChangedLinks, UpdateSim in that order.
ASW exact state bypasses changed-pose tolerance and reads every dynamic link from current engine FrameDataRelativeToWorld.
UpdateSim calls UpdateCollisions before returning, after current link and joint components are written.
UpdateCollisions queries GetContactsFromLastStep after the current world Step and assigns contact component data.
Installed framework contract: PreUpdate then Update physics, then readonly PostUpdate; simTime is time reached after current step.
Bridge PostUpdate writes state and contacts under one mutex; reads current ECM state and ContactSensorData.
SetData always assigns new component data, even if equality returns true. contactsEql position-only tolerance affects changeflag, not force value seen by direct component read.

qualifications: DART solves contacts before position integration. A poststep pose and collision point used in that same step are not simultaneous geometric configurations; this is not a one-step publication delay.
Published contact force is world-frame force on the corresponding first body, derived from perstep constraint impulse divided bydt; previous force-source proof retains collision-order qualification.
The fixed registered midpoint COM plus prior/post sensitivities should remain. Do not choose a lag or origin because it improves closure.
Discrete multibody integration, moving geometry, model/compiled-engine differences and message mapping/completeness remain possible residual sources; this source trace doesnot uniquely quantify them.
Source contracts and versioned upstream implementation are not a runtime trace/disassembly proof of the compiledbinary.
